title: Finite bond-spectral pinching and commutant-optimal shell reduction
question: Can the FI-2b shell be reduced using the full spectral commutant of the bond generator, rather than only the coordinate diagonal algebra, while retaining the exact state-weighted commutator bound?

theorem.setting: A finite doubled Hilbert space with faithful reference state omega, any Hermitian bond generator B with spectral projections P_lambda, and any moved collision witness X.
theorem.spectral_pinching: E_B(X)=sum_lambda P_lambda X P_lambda is a unital completely positive idempotent map onto the B-commutant.
theorem.exact_reduction: For X_0=X-Tr(omega X)I and X_perp=X_0-E_B(X_0), [B,X]=[B,X_perp] exactly.
theorem.comparison: When coordinate pinching is also B-commuting, spectral pinching is the Hilbert--Schmidt orthogonal projection onto the larger B-commutant and cannot have a larger unweighted residual. This does not imply weighted-norm monotonicity or any uniform limit.

verification_contract.lean_scope: finite spectral-pinching commutator identity, scalar-centering invariance and residual orthogonality fixture

promotion_boundary: R-364 closes only the finite spectral-commutant reduction and its finite state-weighted Cauchy bound. The off-diagonal weighted norms and finite-time collar remain to be controlled uniformly.
next_action: Stress the spectral residual and its weighted norms at larger cutoffs and volumes, then seek a modular/Lieb--Robinson estimate or record a scoped growth obstruction.
boundary: Finite exact algebra plus finite V=2 Q3 diagnostics. No source/cutoff/volume/prefix/shape-uniform collar, common core, common alpha, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, mass gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A closure follows.
no_overclaim: The bond spectral projection removes every exactly commuting spectral block and minimizes unweighted Hilbert--Schmidt residual, but it does not prove weighted uniformity or physical reconstruction.
